question_text: A perfectly reflecting mirror of mass $m$ and surface area $A$ is exposed to electromagnetic radiation of intensity $I$ on a rough horizontal surface with coefficient of friction $\mu = \frac{1}{3}$ as shown. The minimum value of pulling force required to move the mirror is $\frac{mg}{2}$. The value of $\frac{mgc}{IA}$ (where $c$ is speed of light) is
diagram_description: A block of mass m rests on a rough horizontal surface. Radiation of intensity I is incident vertically downward onto its upper surface of area A. A horizontal pulling force F acts on the block.
solution: The radiation pressure exerted on a perfectly reflecting mirror is $P_{\text{rad}} = \frac{2I}{c}$, giving a downward force $F_{\text{rad}} = \frac{2IA}{c}$. The normal reaction is $N = mg + \frac{2IA}{c}$. The minimum force required to move the mirror is $F = \mu N = \frac{1}{3}\left(mg + \frac{2IA}{c}\right)$. Equating this to $\frac{mg}{2}$, we get $mg + \frac{2IA}{c} = \frac{3}{2}mg \implies \frac{2IA}{c} = \frac{mg}{2} \implies \frac{mgc}{IA} = 4$.

question_text: If in a region, there is a time varying electric field, then which of the following Maxwell's equation will be most suitable?
solution: The Ampere-Maxwell law incorporates displacement current due to a time-varying electric field and is given by $\oint \vec{B}\cdot d\vec{l} = \mu_0\left(i_c + i_d\right) = \mu_0\left[ i + \varepsilon_0 \frac{d\Phi_E}{dt} \right]$.

question_text: The amplitude of electric field in an electromagnetic wave at a distance $r$ from a point source of power $P$ is (taking efficiency $100\%$)
solution: The intensity at distance $r$ from an isotropic source is $I = \frac{P}{4\pi r^2}$. The intensity in terms of the electric field amplitude $E_0$ is $I = \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 E_0^2 c$. Equating the two expressions gives $\frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 E_0^2 c = \frac{P}{4\pi r^2} \implies E_0 = \sqrt{\frac{P}{2\pi r^2 \varepsilon_0 c}}$.

question_text: In an electromagnetic wave, the effective value of electric field is $100\text{ V/m}$. The intensity of the wave is
solution: The intensity of an electromagnetic wave is given by $I = \varepsilon_0 E_{\text{rms}}^2 c$. Substituting the values: $I = 8.854 \times 10^{-12} \times (100)^2 \times 3 \times 10^8 \approx 26.55\text{ W/m}^2 \approx 26.5\text{ W/m}^2$.

question_text: A parallel plate capacitor consists of two circular plates each of radius $2\text{ cm}$ separated by distance of $0.1\text{ m}$. If voltage across the plates is varying at a rate of $5 \times 10^{13}\text{ V/s}$, then value of displacement current is
solution: Displacement current is $I_d = C \frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d} \frac{dV}{dt}$. Here, $A = \pi r^2 = \pi (0.02)^2 = 4\pi \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}^2$, $d = 0.1\text{ m}$, and $\frac{dV}{dt} = 5 \times 10^{13}\text{ V/s}$. Thus, $I_d = \frac{8.854 \times 10^{-12} \times 4\pi \times 10^{-4}}{0.1} \times 5 \times 10^{13} \approx 5.56\text{ A}$.

question_text: The energy of a photon of EM radiation is of the order of $15\text{ keV}$. To which part of spectrum does it belong?
solution: The wavelength is $\lambda = \frac{hc}{E} = \frac{12400\text{ eV}\cdot\text{\AA}}{15000\text{ eV}} \approx 0.83\text{ \AA} = 0.083\text{ nm}$. This wavelength corresponds to the X-ray region of the electromagnetic spectrum (typically $0.01\text{ nm}$ to $10\text{ nm}$).
